- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 77.5+ values), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after high peaks, but fails to fully revert to historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–3 days after true price peaks.
- High volatility in model forecasts correlates with low correlation to true outcomes — model reacts too aggressively to short-term noise.
- Model underestimates late-period price surges (last 5–10 days of forecast) — especially when true values exceed 80.00.
- Model exhibits “early overconfidence” — first 3–5 forecast days are typically 2–4% higher than true values.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in late history — often underestimates sharp drops or flat periods.
- When history shows strong downward trend, model tends to overestimate recovery or underestimate continuation.
- Model is sensitive to recent high values — overweights recent spikes, leading to overestimation of future prices.
